findings.claim: the local tactics (meeting format, story decomposition, refinement cadence, specific Definition of Done) are explicitly the team's to set
findings.failure_mode: 'explicitly' overstates what the Guide leaves local
findings.evidence: Deep ref L141: only the Daily Scrum's structure is explicitly the Developers' ('The Developers can select whatever structure and techniques they want'). L129: how items become an Increment is 'at the sole discretion of the Developers'. L217: the team creates a DoD only where no organisational standard exists. The Guide says nothing about refinement cadence beyond 'ongoing' (L179) and nothing about other events' formats.
findings.fix: correct: But much is left local: the Daily Scrum's structure is the Developers' to choose, how selected items become an Increment is "at the sole discretion of the Developers" [V], and the team creates its own DoD where no organisational standard exists.

findings.claim: organisational-standard DoD when standards exist (compliance, security, multi-team coordination); team-authored DoD otherwise
findings.failure_mode: two Guide rules conflated
findings.evidence: Deep ref L217: organisational standard, which all teams follow as a minimum. L219 is a separate rule: multiple Scrum Teams on one product 'must mutually define and comply with the same Definition of Done'; that DoD is defined by the teams, not set as an organisational standard.
findings.fix: correct: organisational-standard DoD when standards exist (compliance, security); a DoD the teams mutually define when several Scrum Teams share a product; team-authored DoD otherwise.

findings.claim: "describes a future state of the product which can serve as a target for the Scrum Team to plan against... It is the long-term objective for the Scrum Team. They must fulfill (or abandon) one objective before taking on the next"
findings.failure_mode: quotation altered and unmarked
findings.evidence: Deep ref L183, L190 (both [V]): the source reads 'The Product Goal is the long-term objective for the Scrum Team', not 'It is'. The quote carries no marker.
findings.fix: correct: restore 'The Product Goal is the long-term objective for the Scrum Team' and re-mark: [V]

findings.claim: The order matters: value before scope before plan.
findings.failure_mode: sequencing rule added to the source
findings.evidence: Deep ref L123-131: Sprint Planning 'addresses the following topics'; the Guide does not say they run in order, and requires only that the Sprint Goal be 'finalized prior to the end of Sprint Planning' (L125).
findings.fix: correct: The Guide numbers the Topics why, what, how; the Sprint Goal must be finalised before Sprint Planning ends.

findings.claim: the framework requires hiring for cross-functionality and self-management, not for purely-specialist or purely-managed work. Hiring patterns that select for narrow specialism create framework-fit problems.
findings.failure_mode: team-level property read as an individual hiring criterion
findings.evidence: Deep ref L60: cross-functional means 'the members have all the skills necessary' (collectively). L31: Scrum 'engages groups of people who collectively have all the skills and expertise to do the work and share or acquire such skills as needed'. The Guide says nothing about hiring and does not exclude specialists from a cross-functional team.
findings.fix: correct: the framework requires the team, collectively, to hold every skill the work needs ("groups of people who collectively have all the skills and expertise to do the work and share or acquire such skills as needed" [V]); hiring should close the team's skill gaps and favour people who share or acquire skills.

findings.claim: The Scrum Master is responsible for "Leading, training, and coaching the organization ... Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams"
findings.failure_mode: verbatim quotation carries no marker
findings.evidence: Deep ref L94 carries this list as [V]; the quote matches the source.
findings.fix: re-mark: [V]

findings.claim: are Developers "negotiating the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint without affecting the Sprint Goal"?
findings.failure_mode: quotation altered and unmarked
findings.evidence: Deep ref L200 [V]: 'they collaborate with the Product Owner to negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint without affecting the Sprint Goal'. 'negotiate' became 'negotiating'; no marker.
findings.fix: correct: are Developers collaborating with the Product Owner "to negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint without affecting the Sprint Goal" [V]?

findings.claim: or for narrow specialism the framework cannot absorb?
findings.failure_mode: question rests on the team-vs-individual misreading in D005
findings.evidence: Deep ref L31, L60 as for D005.
findings.fix: correct: Is the hire closing a skill gap in the team, and is the person willing to share or acquire skills as needed?

findings.claim: "The Scrum Master serves the organization in several ways, including: Leading, training, and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption; Planning and advising Scrum implementations within the organization."
findings.failure_mode: verbatim quotation carries no marker
findings.evidence: Source L354-359; deep ref L94 [V].
findings.fix: re-mark: [V]

findings.claim: "shorter Sprints can be employed to generate more learning cycles and limit risk of cost and effort to a smaller time frame"
findings.failure_mode: verbatim quotation carries no marker
findings.evidence: Deep ref L111 [V]; matches source L400-406.
findings.fix: re-mark: [V]

findings.claim: Author cross-team compliance posture as organisational-standard DoD | "If there are multiple Scrum Teams working together on a product, they must mutually define and comply with the same Definition of Done." [V]
findings.failure_mode: quote supports a different Guide rule than the Need cell names
findings.evidence: Deep ref L217 (organisational standard) vs L219 (teams mutually define a shared DoD). The quote is the second rule; the Need names the first.
findings.fix: correct: Need 'Author cross-team compliance posture as a shared DoD', or pair the organisational-standard Need with "If the Definition of Done for an increment is part of the standards of the organization, all Scrum Teams must follow it as a minimum" [V].

findings.claim: only the PO can; only if the Sprint Goal is obsolete.
findings.failure_mode: sufficient condition hardened into necessary condition
findings.evidence: Deep ref L115: 'A Sprint could be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete'. The Guide does not say 'only if'.
findings.fix: correct: only the PO can, and the Guide's named ground is an obsolete Sprint Goal.

findings.claim: The Scrum Guide pushes back on this in two specific ways.
findings.failure_mode: count does not match the enumeration that follows
findings.evidence: The example then lists First (L179), Second (L181) and Third (L183).
findings.fix: correct: in three specific ways.

findings.claim: the founder commits to a DoD update that names the reliability bar as an organisational standard, with the Product Owner authoring the specific change at the next refinement session
findings.failure_mode: DoD authorship and venue misassigned
findings.evidence: Deep ref L217: an organisational-standard DoD is set by the organisation; otherwise 'the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done'. The PO has no DoD-authoring accountability (L74). Refinement concerns Product Backlog items (L179); the DoD is inspected at the Sprint Retrospective (L159).
findings.fix: correct: the founder commits to making the reliability bar an organisational standard that "all Scrum Teams must follow ... as a minimum" [V], with the Scrum Team bringing its own DoD up to it at the next Sprint Retrospective.

findings.claim: refinement ... a sharpening operation for ready items, not a holding area for unprioritised work. The PO's ordering decision is the prioritisation gate; refinement is downstream of it.
findings.failure_mode: source definition reversed
findings.evidence: Deep ref L177: items 'usually acquire this degree of transparency [ready] after refining activities', so refinement is how items become ready, not an operation on ready items. L179: refinement 'is an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size', so ordering is part of refinement, not upstream of it.
findings.fix: correct: The framework names refinement as "the act of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items into smaller more precise items" [V], "an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size" [V]. It is how items become ready. An unbounded backlog that is never ordered is a failure of the Product Owner's ordering accountability, not a use of refinement.

findings.claim: Distinguish the PO's prioritisation decision (ordering) from the team's refinement work (sharpening) explicitly.
findings.failure_mode: follow-up rests on the contradicted premise in D015
findings.evidence: Deep ref L179: order is one of the details refinement adds; L74: the PO is accountable for ordering.
findings.fix: correct: Make the Product Owner's accountability for the order visible in refinement; archive items that never earn a place in the order.

findings.claim: The framework concentrates the most disruptive product decision in one role for a reason: the cancellation has implications for product value the PO is accountable for.
findings.failure_mode: rationale attributed to the framework
findings.evidence: Deep ref L115 states the rule with no rationale; L74 states the PO's value accountability separately. The link is the distillation's inference.
findings.fix: correct: The Guide reserves cancellation to the Product Owner, the person accountable for maximising product value; routing the decision through the founder or board breaks that accountability.

findings.claim: Either hold the DoD and let the date slip (the framework's stance), or update the DoD explicitly so the bar matches what's being shipped (transparent).
findings.failure_mode: second option presented as framework-compatible without the Guide's quality constraint
findings.evidence: Deep ref L109: during the Sprint 'Quality does not decrease'; L210: the DoD describes 'the quality measures required for the product'. Lowering the DoD to match shipped work runs against both. The same move appears at L129.
findings.fix: correct: Hold the DoD and let the date slip (the framework's stance: "Quality does not decrease" [V]). If the organisation decides the bar was wrong, change it openly between Sprints; covert weakening is the position to avoid.

findings.claim: The lens reads the DoD not as a quality bar but as the team's repeatable gate against backlog grooming becoming the operating model. A team with a sharp DoD has the prioritisation gate at the right structural level.
findings.failure_mode: lens redefines a source concept against its definition
findings.evidence: Deep ref L210: the DoD 'is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product'. Prioritisation is the Product Owner's ordering (L74). The DoD is a quality bar by definition and is not a prioritisation gate.
findings.fix: correct: The lens reads the DoD as the team's repeatable quality gate: work that fails it "cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review" [V]. Prioritisation stays with the Product Owner's ordering.

findings.claim: Demand gating: the DoD is the framework's most direct demand-gating mechanism at the work-unit level.
findings.failure_mode: same DoD-as-demand-gate reading as D019
findings.evidence: Deep ref L210, L215: the DoD gates quality and release, not demand intake. Demand is shaped by Product Owner ordering (L74, L80).
findings.fix: correct: Demand gating: Product Owner ordering is the framework's demand gate; the DoD is its quality gate.

findings.claim: Jones reads Agile and Scrum critically: the post-1980 evidence collapse means many software-engineering claims (including Agile claims) are folklore-laden.
findings.failure_mode: other source's position overstated
findings.evidence: jones-evidence-based-sweng-deep.md L149: 'The rarity of measurement data for any of the agile processes means this evidence-based book has little to say about them' [V]. Scrum does not appear in the Jones deep ref; its folklore examples (L15, L39-41) are the 28-to-1 claim and Halstead/McCabe metrics. The bi-exponential fault-report pattern (L165) and estimation material do hold.
findings.fix: correct: Jones sets Agile aside for lack of data ('The rarity of measurement data for any of the agile processes means this evidence-based book has little to say about them' [V]) and does not discuss Scrum.

findings.claim: Mintzberg's six organisational structures cover the cross-team and cross-product structures
findings.failure_mode: model attributed to the wrong author
findings.evidence: openstax-principles-management-deep.md L189: 'Six organisational structure types span the mechanistic-organic continuum (Ch 4.3, Exhibit 4.6)' (functional, divisional, geographic, matrix, networked team, virtual), with no Mintzberg attribution. Mintzberg appears in PoM for managerial roles (L33-37).
findings.fix: correct: Principles of Management's six organisational structure types (Ch 4.3: functional, divisional, geographic, matrix, networked team, virtual)

findings.claim: Provides group dynamics, communication networks, conflict, and negotiation theory ... (groupthink, conflict types, communication network patterns)
findings.failure_mode: content attributed to the other source that its deep ref does not carry
findings.evidence: openstax-organizational-behavior-deep.md Part XI (L330-350) covers the communication model, feedback types and Mintzberg's roles; communication networks do not appear in the deep ref or the converted source. Groupthink (L200-204) and conflict types (L434-450) hold.
findings.fix: correct: Provides group dynamics, communication process, conflict, and negotiation theory ... (groupthink, conflict types, the encoding-decoding communication model)

findings.claim: Carries stakeholder theory (Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience, Freeman) ... Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience informs which stakeholders the PO prioritises representing (Business Ethics).
findings.failure_mode: concepts attributed to the wrong corpus source
findings.evidence: openstax-business-ethics-deep.md Part III (L101-126) carries Donaldson-Preston (descriptive/instrumental/normative), Grunig-Hunt categories and a power x interest matrix with exigency; neither Mitchell-Agle-Wood nor Freeman appears in that deep ref. Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience appears in jones-evidence-based-sweng-deep.md L153.
findings.fix: correct: Carries stakeholder theory (Donaldson and Preston's descriptive/instrumental/normative distinction) and a power x interest prioritisation matrix with exigency (Ch 3.2-3.3) ... the power x interest matrix informs which stakeholders the PO prioritises representing.

findings.claim: Kanban offers flow primitives (WIP limits, cycle time, cumulative flow diagrams) that Scrum's iteration model can incorporate
findings.failure_mode: content attributed to the other source that its deep ref does not carry
findings.evidence: open-kanban-deep.md: cycle time and cumulative flow diagrams do not appear. On WIP it says 'Open Kanban does not ask you to limit WIP' (L76); limiting WIP is a consequence of batch-size reduction (L79). The Scrum half (cumulative flows as a forecasting practice) holds (Scrum deep L113).
findings.fix: correct: Open Kanban asks for batch-size reduction, of which limiting WIP is a consequence, plus continuous learning and a holistic view of the system; the Scrum Guide already names cumulative flows among forecasting practices.

findings.claim: for incidents that cross into ... severe consequence (TC 25-20)
findings.failure_mode: other source's scope misstated
findings.evidence: tc-25-20-army-aar-deep.md L11-19: TC 25-20 is about AARs as the keystone of the Army's training-evaluation process; nothing frames it around severe-consequence incidents.
findings.fix: correct: ... structured discovery after training or operational events (TC 25-20)

findings.claim: Route to OpenStax Principles of Management for Mintzberg's six structures.
findings.failure_mode: model attributed to the wrong author
findings.evidence: As for D022: openstax-principles-management-deep.md L189 carries six structure types without Mintzberg attribution.
findings.fix: correct: Route to OpenStax Principles of Management for its six organisational structure types (Ch 4.3).

findings.claim: The Guide uses "stakeholders" without offering Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience or any other prioritisation framework. Route to openstax-business-ethics.
findings.failure_mode: routing implies the wrong source carries the named model
findings.evidence: The absence claim about the Guide holds. Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience is in jones-evidence-based-sweng-deep.md L153, not in openstax-business-ethics-deep.md (which carries a power x interest matrix, L126).
findings.fix: correct: Route to openstax-business-ethics (power x interest prioritisation, Ch 3.3) and to jones-evidence-based-sweng (Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience, Ch 5.4.5).

findings.claim: TKI five modes, BATNA, principled negotiation: these live in OpenStax Organizational Behavior (Ch 14.4) and Business Law.
findings.failure_mode: mis-cited section
findings.evidence: openstax-organizational-behavior-deep.md L442: the five-mode assertiveness x cooperativeness model is Ch 14.2 (Exhibit 14.4), not named TKI; BATNA and principled negotiation are Ch 14.4 (L464).
findings.fix: correct: the five conflict-handling modes (OB Ch 14.2, Exhibit 14.4), BATNA and principled negotiation (OB Ch 14.4), and Business Law

findings.claim: virtually all substantive claims in the deep reference carry [V] markers from direct quotation or close paraphrase
findings.failure_mode: marker contract misdescribed
findings.evidence: [V] marks the author's words verbatim; close paraphrase is [AP]. The deep ref's [V] passages are verbatim quotations.
findings.fix: correct: virtually all substantive claims in the deep reference carry [V] markers on verbatim quotation

notes: All other [V] quotations checked against sources/converted/scrum-guide-2020.md; exact or clean substrings. Timeboxes, team size, three accountabilities and three Topics check. Integration rows that hold: Letaw (methods), Accounting Vol 2 (make-or-buy, CVP, Goldratt TOC), Principles of Marketing (5A, service-profit chain, RATER, buying centre), Business Law (ADR tiers), Entrepreneurship (build-measure-learn, three funding stages), Field Guide, NHS/LFUO. The three lens sections were audited for claims about the Guide only; lens vocabulary itself is out of scope. Most serious: the refinement anti-pattern reverses the Guide's definition (D015) and the CTO lens redefines the DoD as a prioritisation gate (D019). Five verbatim quotations lack a [V] marker or are altered (D003, D006, D007, D009, D010).
